hero.h1: Turn your lesson plans into games your class begs to play
hero.lead: Paste a lesson, upload a PDF or just describe an idea. Oomba’s AI Builder turns it into an interactive game you can run live on the projector or assign to your class.

how.h: From lesson plan to game in three steps
how.lead: No coding and no design skills. If you can describe your lesson, you can make it playable.

s1.p: Paste your lesson text, upload a PDF, a picture or a text file, or describe what your class should practice, in your own words.

s2.p: It writes the game, then playtests it by itself on phone, tablet and desktop sizes. Ask for changes in plain words: “make it harder”, “add a timer”.

s3.p: Host it live on the projector, share it with only your classes, or add it to a lesson with a due date and see every student’s progress.

builder.h: Your lesson in, a real game out
builder.lead: Talk to the Builder like a teaching assistant who happens to make games. It keeps every version, so you can always go back.
builder.msg: Make a game from this lesson for my 4th graders. Ten minutes, three levels, and end with the exit ticket questions.
builder.bot: Done! Version 1 is ready: three levels, easiest first, with the exit ticket at the end. Press Play to try it.
builder.li1: Understands lesson text, PDFs, pictures and text files you upload
builder.li2: Answers in your language, and in each student’s
builder.li3: Playtests every build on phone, tablet and desktop sizes
builder.li4: Private until you share it: just you, your classes or, after a person on our team reviews it, everyone
builder.li5: Students can build too: describing, testing and fixing a game is planning, writing and debugging, without code
builder.shotAlt: The Oomba Studio: the Builder chat on the left says version 2 is ready, and the game runs in a phone-sized preview on the right.
builder.caption: The real Studio: the Builder on the left, your game on the right.

courses.h: Full courses, ready on day one
courses.lead: Short slide decks, quick checks and game missions in one path. Students work at their own pace; you see progress in the gradebook.

nq.name: Number Quest
nq.p: Place value, fractions, measuring, shapes and data along Netville’s Numberworks with Tally the cat. Every step is mapped to the Common Core State Standards for Mathematics.

cs.name: CS Quest
cs.p: A full program a teacher with no computer science background can run: 45-minute lessons, each with a plan, a game chapter, a live warm-up and an exit ticket. CSTA levels 1B and 2.

cd.name: Cyber Defenders
cd.p: How messages travel, how codes protect them, what stays private and how to spot a trick, with Pim the owl at the Netville post office. Every step is mapped to CYBER.ORG standards.

live.lead: Warm-ups and exit tickets your class actually looks forward to. Students join on their own devices with a 7-digit code.
live.li1: Quest Race, Question Battle, Brain Board, Tug of Math and more
live.li2: Use a starter question set, type your own, or let AI draft one for you to edit
live.li3: Scores go straight into your gradebook
live.li4: Signed-in students only: no chat, no typing, no made-up names
live.shotAlt: A live Question Battle lobby: five student avatars wait while the big screen shows the game code and a QR code.

why.h: Fun is the delivery system. Learning is the point.
why.lead: Good learning games lean on a few well-studied ideas from the science of learning.

b1.p: Answering to win pulls knowledge back out of memory, and recalling something is one of the most reliable ways to make it stick.

b2.p: Every answer gets a response in the moment, so mistakes are fixed while the thinking is still fresh.

b3.p: “One more round” feels like play, not a worksheet, so students practice more, without the weight of a grade.

b4.p: A game gives every student a turn, including the ones who rarely raise a hand.

b5.p: To build a game about a topic, students have to understand it well enough to teach it to a computer.

safety.h: Built for classrooms, safe by design
safety.lead: Made for ages 5 to 14, with you in control of your classes.
safety.li1: No ads, and no advertising or tracking cookies
safety.li2: Students never need an email address, and we never ask their age or home address
safety.li3: A student’s real name, if you add one, is seen only by your school’s staff
safety.li4: You approve who joins your classes, and no student can chat with strangers
safety.li5: Every game runs in a locked sandbox, and a person on our team reviews any game before it goes public
safety.li6: What students type is filtered, and pictures they upload are checked and stripped of location data
safety.links: Read how we keep kids safe and our privacy notice.

faq.a1: A game-based learning platform for grades K to 8. Teachers turn their own lessons into interactive games with an AI Builder, run live class games, and use ready-made courses in math, computer science and online safety.
faq.q2: How does the free trial work?
faq.a2: Start a 14-day free trial with no card. Everything in the Teacher plan is included while it runs, and when it ends you decide whether to subscribe.
faq.q3: Do I pay for each student?
faq.a3: No. One yearly price per teacher covers all of your students. There are no per-student fees.
faq.q4: What can I turn into a game?
faq.a4: Almost any lesson: paste the text, upload a PDF, a picture or a text file, or describe the topic and what your class should practice. The Builder uses your material as a reference and makes a game around it.
faq.q5: Do students need an email address?
faq.a5: No. You can make school accounts for your class and print login cards, with no student email needed. Anyone can also play the free games straight away.
faq.q6: Does it work on Chromebooks and iPads?
faq.a6: Yes. It runs in any up-to-date browser on Chromebooks, iPads and other tablets, laptops, phones and interactive boards, with nothing to install.
faq.q7: Is it safe for my students?
faq.a7: It is made for ages 5 to 14: no ads, no tracking cookies, no student emails, no chat with strangers, filtered text, and a person on our team reviews any game before it goes public.
faq.q8: Can our school pay by invoice or purchase order?
faq.a8: Yes. Schools pay the same price per teacher per year, by invoice or purchase order. Email us and we will set it up.
faq.a9: {count} languages, including English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Arabic, Hebrew and Japanese. Each student picks their own, and the Builder answers in it.
